research_question: In people with a naturally acquired common cold, does zinc treatment (oral lozenges, tablets/syrup or intranasal preparations) compared with placebo reduce the mean duration of the cold in days?
treatment_label: Zinc treatment (oral lozenges, tablets/syrup, or intranasal gel/spray) for an active cold
outcome_description: Mean duration of the common cold in days, measured from the start of treatment (or from symptom onset, as defined by each trial) until resolution of the cold / complete symptom clearance. Extracted as group means with SDs (or as a reported mean difference with its variance, or convertible t/F/CI data) and pooled as a mean difference in days. Excludes proportion with ongoing symptoms at a fixed endpoint, symptom severity scores, duration of individual symptoms, adverse events, and prevention/incidence outcomes.
positive_direction: A positive effect size means zinc shortened the common cold — participants receiving zinc recovered in fewer days on average than those receiving placebo.
search_queries: zinc lozenges common cold duration randomized placebo trial
zinc acetate gluconate cold symptoms duration controlled trial
intranasal zinc gluconate common cold treatment trial outcome
inclusion_criteria: Participants had a naturally acquired common cold / upper respiratory infection and treatment began after symptom onset (treatment trials)
Compared any zinc preparation (lozenge, tablet, syrup, intranasal gel or spray) against a placebo or no-zinc control group
Reported some quantitative data on cold duration (mean days to resolution, or data convertible to it)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, opinion piece, theoretical or modelling paper, case report)
No comparison between a zinc treatment condition and a placebo/control condition (single-arm or uncontrolled study)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size for cold duration can be computed (no means with SDs/SEs/CIs, t/F values, or equivalent statistics)

Completely unrelated to zinc treatment of the common cold (e.g. prevention-only trials, experimentally induced rhinovirus challenge studies, zinc for other conditions, or only non-duration outcomes such as severity, adverse events, or proportion still symptomatic)
moderators_to_extract: Zinc formulation (lozenge vs tablet/syrup vs intranasal)
Zinc salt type (acetate, gluconate, sulphate, other)
Time from symptom onset to treatment initiation
Risk of bias / allocation concealment and blinding adequacy
effect_size_note: Pool as a mean difference in days (zinc minus placebo), signed so that a positive pooled value favours zinc (shorter cold). Use random-effects (DerSimonian–Laird or REML) inverse-variance pooling given expected clinical heterogeneity in formulation and dose; where trials report only SEs, CIs, or p-values, back-calculate SDs. Assess heterogeneity with I² and tau², and examine small-study effects with a funnel plot and Egger's test if ≥10 trials contribute.
single_outcome_target: duration of the common cold (days to resolution)
